notes:
Topline: Enterprise contact-center platform building an opinionated agent-assist layer for mid-large customers. Wants live streaming suggestions (token-by-token) inside agent UI + tool-calls to internal CRMs.

Key quotes: "If suggestions lag during peak periods the agents disable the feature — we need sub-100ms suggestion time for first token end-to-end." — VP Eng.

Primary priorities: low-latency streaming, deterministic fallbacks, audit trails for every suggestion, tight guardrails to avoid PII exposure, and predictable per-agent costs.

User/Pain: dropped suggestion feature during Black Friday style spikes; current self-hosted stack can't autoscale fast enough; wasted agent time due to stale suggestions. Cost sensitivity: moderate — will pay for predictability.

Modeling preferences: pref open weights where possible but open to private models if latency/SLOs improve. Prefer routing to cheaper quantized variants for non-live batches.

Integration touches: tool-calling to internal ticketing API, real-time call metadata ingestion, UI streaming hook with optimistic token rendering.

Short items: SSO + SCIM required, retention rules per customer (30/90/365), can host private control plane in VPC or on-prem for strategic customers.

Internal champions: Head of Product (trial), Director of Ops (POC sponsor).

requirements_summary:
Workload: real-time agent assist with streaming token suggestions + synchronous tool-calls (ticket create/update).
Latency SLOs: first token <=100ms E2E at target concurrency; 95th pct <=200ms.
Throughput: support up to 1,200 concurrent agent sessions in peak region, average 2 messages/sec per session.
Reliability: graceful degradation — fallback to cached canned responses or non-streaming model when capacity constrained.
Guardrails: deterministic response filters for PII, must log suggestion provenance (model id, version, prompt hash).
Security: SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, audit logs for suggestions, KMS-managed keys for customer data at rest, data residency controls per customer.
Operational: need per-token cost breakdown, burst capacity plan for flash sales, canary rollouts and instant rollback.
POC scope: 48-hour live POC with production-like traffic ramp to 1.2k concurrent sessions; measure latency distribution, error rates, and cost metrics.
